plan.title: Amazing Apples
plan.weeklyOverview: Toddlers explore real apples through looking, sorting, moving, tasting (with allergy care), and process art. Each day adds one new way to know an apple.
plan.objectives:
Identify apples as a healthy fruit.
Recognize red, green, and yellow apples.
Explore apples using the five senses.
Compare apples by size, color, and texture.
Practice counting, sorting, and matching apples.
Strengthen fine motor skills through art and sensory play.
Build vocabulary related to apples and orchards.
Encourage curiosity through simple science investigations.
Participate in cooperative play and group discussions.
Develop confidence while exploring new foods and experiences.
plan.weeklyMaterials:
Red, green, and yellow apples
Apple slices
Plastic apples
Apple basket
Toy grocery items
Apple tree props
Paint
Construction paper
Glue sticks
Crayons
Dot markers
Apple stickers
Play dough
Sensory bin materials
hand lenses
Books
Music player

Fruit

plan.familyConnection: Invite families to visit a grocery store or orchard together to look for different apples. Encourage children to taste apples at home and talk about their favorite color, taste, and texture.
plan.observationOpportunities:
Color recognition
Counting skills
Vocabulary development
Sensory exploration
Fine motor skills
Social interactions
Curiosity during science activities
plan.adaptations:
Provide adaptive scissors and crayons as needed.
Use picture cards for vocabulary support.
Offer larger manipulatives for children needing additional assistance.
Modify activities based on developmental levels.

monday.theme: Look, Touch, Stamp — Meeting Real Apples
monday.objectives:
Examine whole apples with sight and touch.
Make first stamp prints.
Fill baskets by dots.
Practice gentle picking reaches.
monday.materials:
Whole apples
Apple halves for stamping
Washable paint
Chunky apples
Dot baskets
Paper apple props
monday.vocabulary:
Apple
Red
Green
Yellow
Fruit
Stem

items.title: Apple Investigation
items.objective: Look closely at whole apples using sight, touch, and smell.
items.description: Toddlers examine whole apples at a low table—stem, skin, coolness—without tasting today.
items.materials:
Three whole apples with different skins
Washable placemats
Damp cloth
Optional clear view-finders
items.setup: Place one apple on each placemat with a damp cloth nearby. Keep tasting for Thursday.
items.steps:
1. Invite children to look and gently touch.
2. Narrate stem, skin, cool, bumpy.
3. Offer a view-finder for close looking.
4. End before anyone bites; refrigerate leftovers.
items.teacherRole: Narrate sensory words; redirect bites to look-only; keep groups small.
items.teacherLanguage: Feel the cool skin. Where is the stem? Does it smell sweet?
items.observationOpportunities:
Touches stem or turns the apple
Echoes a sensory word
Accepts look-only boundary
items.extensions: Place one apple on a tray scale and watch the needle move together.
items.adaptations: Offer a sealed clear bag with an apple inside for children who avoid direct touch.
items.safetyNotes: Whole apples only today. Redirect biting. Wash hands after.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand-over-hand gentle touch for brief seconds, then release.
items.additionalChallenge: Ask which apple feels heaviest in two hands.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants may look from a caregiver’s lap; older toddlers lead naming.
items.cleanupTip: Wipe juice rings; refrigerate whole apples for later tasting.

items.title: Apple Stamp Painting
items.objective: Press adult-cut apple halves into washable paint to make prints.
items.description: Process stamping with apple halves—overlapping prints are success.
items.materials:
Adult-cut apple halves
Washable paint
Paper or grocery-bag sheets
Trays
Wipes
items.setup: Cover table; blot each stamp on scrap paper once before children’s paper.
items.steps:
1. Model one press-and-lift.
2. Children stamp freely.
3. Name colors they choose.
4. Set prints to dry.
items.teacherRole: Cut apples beforehand; accept messy overlaps; keep paint away from mouths.
items.teacherLanguage: Press. Lift. Look—your print! Which color next?
items.observationOpportunities:
Press-and-lift vs smear
Color preference
Tolerance for sticky paint
items.extensions: Count how many red prints landed on one page.
items.adaptations: Offer a sponge stamp for children who dislike apple flesh texture.
items.safetyNotes: Adult prepares cuts. Use taste-safe washable paint. Watch mouths.
items.supportAdaptations: Pre-load the stamp; child only presses.
items.additionalChallenge: Try a second color on the same page.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers stamp on large cardboard outdoors.
items.cleanupTip: Soak apple halves for compost; wash trays before paint skins over.

items.title: Count the Apples
items.objective: Fill baskets to match simple dot quantities.
items.description: Toddlers place chunky apples into baskets labeled with dots—not pressured numerals.
items.materials:
Chunky plastic or fabric apples
Baskets with 1–3 dots
Floor space
items.setup: Start with two baskets (1 and 2 dots). Keep extras in a tub.
items.steps:
1. Point to the dots together.
2. Children place apples one by one.
3. Celebrate full and more language.
4. Dump and try again.
items.teacherRole: Honor dump-and-fill play; narrate quantity without drilling.
items.teacherLanguage: How many dots? Can we put one apple for each?
items.observationOpportunities:
One-to-one vs handful dump
Notices fuller basket
Seeks help with dots
items.extensions: Deliver three apples to the dramatic-play market.
items.adaptations: Limit to baskets 1 and 2 only.
items.safetyNotes: Oversized counters only. Sweep floor apples to prevent slips.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher places first apple; child continues.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a 3-dot basket when ready.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers match numeral cards after dots.
items.cleanupTip: Count aloud while returning apples to the bin.

items.title: Pick the Apples
items.objective: Reach for apple props at two heights and carry them to a basket.
items.description: Movement orchard: tape or hang apple shapes low and high; gentle picking.
items.materials:
Paper or fabric apples
Baskets
Tape or low hooks
Optional music
items.setup: Place apples at floor and child-chest height. Clear pathways.
items.steps:
1. Model gentle pick and carry.
2. Children gather apples into baskets.
3. Pause for rest between rounds.
4. Sort into the big orchard tub.
items.teacherRole: Cue gentle hands; stop racing; spot near furniture.
items.teacherLanguage: Reach high. Soft pick. Two hands on the basket.
items.observationOpportunities:
Prefers low or high apples
Carry style
Stops when music pauses
items.extensions: Sort picked apples by color at the finish.
items.adaptations: Seated pick from a low crate for less locomotion.
items.safetyNotes: No climbing furniture. Keep pathways clear.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand a low apple directly; celebrate the carry.
items.additionalChallenge: Carry two apples without dropping.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers hang a few apples for friends.
items.cleanupTip: Two orchard helpers gather leftovers.

monday.teacherPreparation: Allergy list posted for Thursday. Adult-cut stamp apples before arrival. Stage investigation table fully.
monday.circleTime: Sing Crunch Goes the Apple once. Pass one whole apple for look-only. Preview stamp and pick games.
monday.activityFlow: Investigation → Stamp Painting → Count the Apples → Pick the Apples (short outdoor/indoor reach).
monday.questions: What do you notice on the apple? Is the skin cool or warm?
monday.observationFocus: Sensory approach or avoidance; gentle hands; dump-vs-place counting.
monday.familyConnection: Ask families to notice one grocery apple color or stem at home and share a word.
monday.outdoorPlay: Hang fabric apples on a low fence for gentle picking; shade for sticky stamp cleanup.
monday.observations: Notes who needs dry alternatives; who uses stem/skin words.
monday.adaptations: Sealed-bag apple for touch-averse children; seated pick option.
monday.safetyNotes: No tasting Monday. Adult prepares stamp cuts.

tuesday.theme: Colors We Can Sort, Tear, and Dance
tuesday.objectives:
Sort red/green/yellow props.
Tear paper for a process collage.
Freeze on color cues.
tuesday.materials:
Color baskets
Paper circles or props
Tear paper
Glue sticks
Scarves
tuesday.vocabulary:
Red
Green
Yellow
Apple
Color
Sort

items.title: Apple Color Sort
items.objective: Sort red, green, and yellow apple props into matching baskets.
items.description: Sample apple in each basket anchors the first sort.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow apple props or paper circles
Three baskets with color swatches
items.setup: Place one sample apple in each basket before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Name the sample colors.
2. Children sort remaining apples.
3. Narrate mismatches kindly.
4. Mix and sort again.
items.teacherRole: Accept size sorts first, then invite a color pass.
items.teacherLanguage: Does it match the sample? Red with red.
items.observationOpportunities:
Checks sample before placing
Strategy when one color runs out
items.extensions: Sort with eyes closed using textured paper apples.
items.adaptations: Begin with two colors only.
items.safetyNotes: No tiny sorting chips. Real apples are look-only during sort.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand the child only red apples first.
items.additionalChallenge: Add yellow on round two.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers label baskets with words.
items.cleanupTip: Sing a short apples-home chant into the storage tub.

items.title: Apple Peel Tear Collage
items.objective: Tear paper and stick pieces to build a process apple collage.
items.description: Children tear red, green, and yellow paper and glue pieces onto a soft circle guide—or ignore the guide.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow paper
Glue sticks
Trays
Optional light pencil circle
items.setup: Start one teacher tear on each tray. Glue sticks only.
items.steps:
1. Model a slow tear.
2. Children tear and stick freely.
3. Optional: add a brown paper stem.
4. Display process work—no matching model.
items.teacherRole: Protect tearing as the skill; refuse pre-cut squares as the main task.
items.teacherLanguage: Tear, tear—stick. Your apple can be messy!
items.observationOpportunities:
Tear style
Clusters vs covers
Asks for more paper
items.extensions: Dictate a one-word title for the collage.
items.adaptations: Pre-snipped starter tears; child continues tearing.
items.safetyNotes: No glitter. Watch paper near mouths.
items.supportAdaptations: Hold the paper while the child pulls.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a leaf torn from green paper.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers tear magazine color patches.
items.cleanupTip: Keep a scrap bowl for tomorrow’s collage.

items.title: Apple Color Dance
items.objective: Move or freeze when a color scarf cue is shown.
items.description: Short color-cue freezes with scarves—20–30 second rounds.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow scarves or bandanas
Clear floor space
items.setup: Give each child one scarf color. Tape a dance circle if needed.
items.steps:
1. Hold up a color cue.
2. Matching scarves move; others freeze.
3. Switch cues quickly.
4. End with all colors dancing.
items.teacherRole: Keep rounds short; model exaggerated freeze.
items.teacherLanguage: Red moves! Green freezes. Listen with your eyes.
items.observationOpportunities:
Watches cue before moving
Freeze quality
Frustration with waiting
items.extensions: Add a drum tap for each color change.
items.adaptations: Partner a hesitant child with a teacher model.
items.safetyNotes: Scarves off necks. Clear furniture edges.
items.supportAdaptations: Only two colors in the first round.
items.additionalChallenge: Children take turns being the color caller.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers all move together without freeze.
items.cleanupTip: Toss scarves into a laundry basket like apple collecting.

tuesday.teacherPreparation: Print/cut color cards from the picture pack. Pre-tear one sample strip per tray.
tuesday.circleTime: Hold up three color cards. Children point to matching clothes or scarves.
tuesday.activityFlow: Color Sort → Apple Peel Tear Collage → Apple Color Dance.
tuesday.questions: Which basket matches this apple? What color did you tear first?
tuesday.observationFocus: Color matching strategy; tear strength; freeze control.
tuesday.familyConnection: Send a photo of the collage process (faces optional).
tuesday.outdoorPlay: Sidewalk chalk color circles as sort targets.
tuesday.observations: Who sorts by size first; who needs two-color start.
tuesday.adaptations: Two colors only for first sort; starter tears for collage.
tuesday.safetyNotes: Glue sticks only; scarves off necks.

wednesday.objectives:
Compare apple sizes.
Measure with yarn/cubes.
Roll bodies safely on mats.
wednesday.materials:
Sized apple props
Yarn
Cubes
Mats or blankets
wednesday.vocabulary:
Big
Small
Large
Little
Round
Compare

items.title: Big or Small?
items.objective: Compare clearly different apple sizes and sort into big/small.
items.description: Side-by-side size compare with obvious contrast before close calls.
items.materials:
Large and small apple props
Two baskets labeled with big/little circles
items.setup: Start with extreme size pairs only.
items.steps:
1. Hold two apples side by side.
2. Children choose big or small basket.
3. Invite disagreement and re-check.
4. Line biggest to smallest.
items.teacherRole: Welcome debate; avoid saying a child is wrong about close sizes.
items.teacherLanguage: Which feels bigger in your hands? Show me.
items.observationOpportunities:
Sight vs hand-weigh strategy
Invented size words
items.extensions: Build a bridge from biggest to smallest.
items.adaptations: Offer only two objects at a time.
items.safetyNotes: No hard throwing of real apples.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher holds both; child points.
items.additionalChallenge: Find a medium apple for a third basket.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers measure with yarn length.
items.cleanupTip: Store big and small in separate bins.

items.title: Apple Measuring Station
items.objective: Measure around or beside apples using yarn and cubes.
items.description: Non-standard measurement: wrap yarn or line cubes beside an apple.
items.materials:
Apples or props
Short yarn lengths
Linking cubes or Duplo
Trays
items.setup: Demonstrate wrapping yarn once, then hand yarn to the child.
items.steps:
1. Wrap or line up units.
2. Count cubes with pointing.
3. Compare which apple needs longer yarn.
4. Reset trays.
items.teacherRole: Hold apple steady when needed; keep yarn short.
items.teacherLanguage: Around the apple—how many cubes tall beside it?
items.observationOpportunities:
Yarn taut vs loose
One-to-one pointing on cubes
items.extensions: Graph longer/shorter with cube towers.
items.adaptations: Teacher wraps; child chooses which apple is longer.
items.safetyNotes: Yarn under 12 inches. Adult supervision.
items.supportAdaptations: Clip yarn to tray edge.
items.additionalChallenge: Measure a toy pumpkin vs apple.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers record tally marks.
items.cleanupTip: Wind yarn onto cardboard notches.

items.title: Roll Like an Apple
items.objective: Practice log rolls and curled rolls on mats.
items.description: Gross-motor apple play: log roll first, then curled apple roll.
items.materials:
Gym mats or folded blankets
Optional bean bags
Clear roll path
items.setup: Clear the path. Offer log rolls before curled rolls.
items.steps:
1. Model log roll.
2. Children roll across the mat.
3. Optional bean bag on belly.
4. Rest and try curled rolls.
items.teacherRole: Spot near walls; no head-first dives.
items.teacherLanguage: Curl small like an apple. Roll, roll—stop!
items.observationOpportunities:
Initiates vs waits
Head protection
Enjoys vs avoids floor
items.extensions: Roll to a basket and drop in one apple prop.
items.adaptations: Seated spin for children avoiding floor rolls.
items.safetyNotes: Clear path. Spot near walls. No diving.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand cue on shoulder to start roll.
items.additionalChallenge: Roll carrying a soft apple to the basket.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers rock side to side only.
items.cleanupTip: Two children stack mats from opposite ends.

wednesday.teacherPreparation: Cut yarn under 12 inches. Clear roll path. Set measuring trays.
wednesday.circleTime: Read or revisit Ten Apples Up On Top! with finger counting.
wednesday.activityFlow: Big or Small? → Apple Measuring Station → Roll Like an Apple.
wednesday.questions: Which apple needs the longer yarn? How do we keep heads safe when we roll?
wednesday.observationFocus: Size language; measuring attempts; roll initiation.
wednesday.familyConnection: Invite families to compare two fruits by size at home.
wednesday.outdoorPlay: Compare pinecones as big/small orchard props on dry grass.
wednesday.observations: Who debates size; who avoids floor rolls.
wednesday.safetyNotes: Short yarn; spot rolls near walls.

thursday.theme: Taste, Vote, and Open the Market
thursday.objectives:
Taste safely or help as non-taster.
Vote on a favorite graph.
Play apple market roles.
thursday.materials:
Allergy list
Tiny apple bits
Napkins
Graph paper
Market props
thursday.vocabulary:
Taste
Sweet
Crunchy
Juicy
Favorite
Healthy

items.title: Apple Taste Test
items.objective: Taste tiny apple pieces safely—or take a non-tasting helper role.
items.description: Allergy-aware tasting with equal status for non-tasters.
items.materials:
Adult-cut pea-sized apple bits
Color-coded napkins
Allergy list
Graph stickers
items.setup: Review allergy notes. Plate tiny bits. Offer smell plate for non-tasters.
items.steps:
1. Wash hands.
2. Smell, then optional taste.
3. Non-tasters serve napkins or place stickers.
4. Name sweet/tart favorites.
items.teacherRole: Guard allergy protocol; never pressure tasting.
items.teacherLanguage: Smell first. One tiny bite if you want. Helpers are important too.
items.observationOpportunities:
Spit/swallow/hold
Chooses helper role
Points to favorite napkin
items.extensions: Place sticker on class favorite chart.
items.adaptations: Lick a clean spoon that touched apple for texture-sensitive children.
items.safetyNotes: Allergy protocol first. Adult prepares cuts. Watch each bite. No sharing bites.
items.supportAdaptations: Smell-only plate with equal celebration.
items.additionalChallenge: Describe tart vs sweet to a friend.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help pass napkins.
items.cleanupTip: Compost scraps; sanitize table twice.

items.title: Favorite Apple Graph
items.objective: Place a sticker on a favorite apple-color column—including non-tasters.
items.description: Picture-card headers; every child votes, including look-only choosers.
items.materials:
Butcher paper columns
Apple color picture cards
Stickers
items.setup: Post three columns with picture-card headers—not children’s faces.
items.steps:
1. Review colors.
2. Each child places one sticker.
3. Count the tallest column together.
4. Photograph for families.
items.teacherRole: Include non-tasters in ‘looks yummy’ columns; avoid pressure.
items.teacherLanguage: Which column is yours today? Let’s clap for the tallest.
items.observationOpportunities:
Counts spontaneously
Changes mind after peers
Includes non-taster role
items.extensions: Clap once per sticker in the tallest column.
items.adaptations: Offer hand-over-hand sticker placement when fine motor is emerging.
items.safetyNotes: Stickers off mouths. Avoid food-look stickers.
items.supportAdaptations: Offer only two columns.
items.additionalChallenge: Children dictate a caption for the graph photo.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers write tallies.
items.cleanupTip: Photograph, then roll the paper.

items.title: Apple Market
items.objective: Buy and sell apple props using simple polite phrases.
items.description: Small stocked stand so children practice restocking, not hoarding.
items.materials:
Toy or fabric apples
Baskets
Muffin-tin drawer
Paper coin circles
items.setup: Stock only a few apples. Model one phrase, then step out.
items.steps:
1. Open the market.
2. Take turns as seller/customer.
3. Restock from the orchard tub.
4. Close with a sold-out sign.
items.teacherRole: Model ‘How many apples today?’ once; coach turn-taking.
items.teacherLanguage: How many apples today? Please. Thank you.
items.observationOpportunities:
Role preference
Turn-taking at register
Uses please/thank you
items.extensions: Deliver a basket to block-area neighbors.
items.adaptations: Picture menu for pointing orders.
items.safetyNotes: Coins larger than choke tubes. No real coins.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher plays customer first.
items.additionalChallenge: Price apples as 1 or 2 coins.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers write open/closed signs.
items.cleanupTip: Sort props by type under the sold-out sign.

thursday.teacherPreparation: Confirm allergies. Cut pea-sized bits. Post graph with picture-card headers.
thursday.activityFlow: Taste Test → Favorite Apple Graph → Apple Market.
thursday.questions: Sweet or tart? Which column gets your sticker today?
thursday.observationFocus: Tasting comfort; equal helper status; market turn-taking.
thursday.familyConnection: Share graph photo and one tasting word (or helper pride note).
thursday.outdoorPlay: Blanket market under a tree with wagon deliveries.
thursday.observations: Who chooses helper role; polite phrases at market.
thursday.adaptations: Smell-only plate; picture menu for orders.
thursday.safetyNotes: Allergy protocol; no sharing bites; oversized coins.

friday.objectives:
Order growth cards.
Look at seeds safely.
Make process trees.
Celebrate with a short parade.
friday.materials:
Growth cards
Apple half for looking
Seed jar
Tree art supplies
Scarves
friday.vocabulary:
Tree
Orchard
Branch
Leaf
Blossom
Seed
Grow
Harvest

items.title: Apple Life Cycle
items.objective: Put apple growth cards in order from seed to ripe apple.
items.description: Left-to-right story with picture-card pack growth sequence.
items.materials:
Amazing Apples growth cards
Tray
Optional painter’s tape arrow
items.setup: Show order once, mix cards, invite repair of the story.
items.steps:
1. Say the story together.
2. Mix cards.
3. Children reorder.
4. Act out seed-to-tree with bodies.
items.teacherRole: Keep language story-like; avoid quiz pressure.
items.teacherLanguage: What comes after the seed? Then the little tree…
items.observationOpportunities:
Places seed before tree
Story language while ordering
items.extensions: Match cards to a real potted seedling if available.
items.adaptations: Offer first/last cards only; adult fills middle with child approval.
items.safetyNotes: Laminate cards. No loose seeds as manipulatives.
items.supportAdaptations: Two-card choice only.
items.additionalChallenge: Child teaches the order to a friend.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers add blossom card.
items.cleanupTip: Rubber-band each set in order.

items.title: Apple Seed Discovery
items.objective: Look at seeds inside an adult-cut apple half.
items.description: Supervised looking: adult cuts and holds; seeds go into a sealed jar after.
items.materials:
Adult-cut apple half
Observation tray
Sealed clear jar
Optional view-finder
items.setup: Cut away from children. Display half on tray; jar ready for seeds.
items.steps:
1. Look and point.
2. Count seeds together if calm.
3. Seal seeds in the jar.
4. Compost the fruit scrap.
items.teacherRole: Keep tools away from children; narrate inside/outside.
items.teacherLanguage: The seeds were inside. We look—we don’t eat the seeds.
items.observationOpportunities:
Points without grabbing
Compares to other seeds known
items.extensions: Plant one seed in a cup for a week-long watch.
items.adaptations: Dry picture card for children who dislike wet fruit.
items.safetyNotes: Adult prepares the cut away from children. Seeds are not snacks.
items.supportAdaptations: Watch from a second chair with the picture card.
items.additionalChallenge: Draw the seed jar in a science journal.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help wipe the tray.
items.cleanupTip: Seal seeds; sanitize tools away from children.

items.title: My Apple Tree
items.objective: Build a process apple tree with trunk and fingerprint or pom-pom apples.
items.description: Child-taped trunk strip plus messy apples—no identical sticker rows.
items.materials:
Brown paper trunk strips
Green paper or paint
Red fingerprint paint or large pom-poms
Glue
items.setup: Offer trunks children tape themselves. Put out fingerprint pads or pom-poms.
items.steps:
1. Tape trunk.
2. Add leaves.
3. Add apples freely.
4. Dictate a one-line story.
items.teacherRole: Refuse adult-perfect trees; celebrate all-over apples.
items.teacherLanguage: Where will your apples grow? Top, bottom, everywhere?
items.observationOpportunities:
Apples only at top vs all over
Narrates pickers
items.extensions: Family caption from dictated story.
items.adaptations: Larger pom-poms for grasp.
items.safetyNotes: Washable non-toxic paint. Pom-poms larger than choke tubes.
items.supportAdaptations: Pre-taped trunk; child adds apples only.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a sun or basket under the tree.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers tear leaves themselves.
items.cleanupTip: Close paint pads; pom-poms in mesh wash bag.

items.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
items.objective: Share one apple word and parade once around the rug.
items.description: Closing circle: vocabulary share, short parade, scarf or streamer wave.
items.materials:
Scarves or streamers
Optional music or LLH chant
Graph photo
items.setup: Keep parade path to one rug loop.
items.steps:
1. Each child shares one apple word (opt-in).
2. Chant together.
3. One loop parade.
4. Wave to the graph photo.
items.teacherRole: Keep energy walking-feet; honor silent waves.
items.teacherLanguage: What apple word will you share? Harvest parade—walking feet.
items.observationOpportunities:
Which words return
Who wants to lead
Regulation in parade
items.extensions: Thank kitchen staff who washed apples.
items.adaptations: Flag wave from a chair instead of marching.
items.safetyNotes: No running parade. Streamers away from faces.
items.supportAdaptations: Whisper share to teacher only.
items.additionalChallenge: Child leads one verse of the chant.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce with scarves in arms.
items.cleanupTip: End with graph/art photo for families.

friday.teacherPreparation: Rubber-band card sets. Cut apple away from children. Stage art.
friday.circleTime: Retell seed-to-apple with cards. Practice harvest chant.
friday.activityFlow: Life Cycle → Seed Discovery → My Apple Tree → Harvest Celebration.
friday.questions: What comes after the seed? What apple word will you share?
friday.observationFocus: Sequencing language; look-only seed safety; parade regulation.
friday.familyConnection: Send tree art photo and favorite vocabulary from the week.
friday.outdoorPlay: Parade to the garden fence and back; match cards to a seedling if present.
friday.observations: Who retells growth order; who leads parade calmly.
friday.adaptations: First/last cards only; chair flag wave.
friday.safetyNotes: Adult cut only; seeds sealed; walking feet in parade.

2. Narrate stem, skin, cool, bumpy.

4. End before anyone bites; refrigerate leftovers.
items.teacherRole: Narrate sensory words; redirect bites to look-only; keep groups small.
items.teacherLanguage: Feel the cool skin. Where is the stem? Does it smell sweet?
items.observationOpportunities:
Touches stem or turns the apple
Echoes a sensory word
Accepts look-only boundary
items.extensions: Place one apple on a tray scale and watch the needle move together.
items.adaptations: Offer a sealed clear bag with an apple inside for children who avoid direct touch.
items.safetyNotes: Whole apples only today. Redirect biting. Wash hands after.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand-over-hand gentle touch for brief seconds, then release.
items.additionalChallenge: Ask which apple feels heaviest in two hands.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants may look from a caregiver’s lap; older toddlers lead naming.
items.cleanupTip: Wipe juice rings; refrigerate whole apples for later tasting.

items.title: Apple Stamp Painting
items.objective: Press adult-cut apple halves into washable paint to make prints.
items.description: Process stamping with apple halves—overlapping prints are success.
items.materials:
Adult-cut apple halves
Washable paint
Paper or grocery-bag sheets
Trays
Wipes
items.setup: Cover table; blot each stamp on scrap paper once before children’s paper.
items.steps:
1. Model one press-and-lift.
2. Children stamp freely.
3. Name colors they choose.
4. Set prints to dry.
items.teacherRole: Cut apples beforehand; accept messy overlaps; keep paint away from mouths.
items.teacherLanguage: Press. Lift. Look—your print! Which color next?
items.observationOpportunities:
Press-and-lift vs smear
Color preference
Tolerance for sticky paint
items.extensions: Count how many red prints landed on one page.
items.adaptations: Offer a sponge stamp for children who dislike apple flesh texture.
items.safetyNotes: Adult prepares cuts. Use taste-safe washable paint. Watch mouths.
items.supportAdaptations: Pre-load the stamp; child only presses.
items.additionalChallenge: Try a second color on the same page.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers stamp on large cardboard outdoors.
items.cleanupTip: Soak apple halves for compost; wash trays before paint skins over.

items.title: Count the Apples
items.objective: Fill baskets to match simple dot quantities.
items.description: Toddlers place chunky apples into baskets labeled with dots—not pressured numerals.
items.materials:
Chunky plastic or fabric apples
Baskets with 1–3 dots
Floor space
items.setup: Start with two baskets (1 and 2 dots). Keep extras in a tub.
items.steps:
1. Point to the dots together.
2. Children place apples one by one.
3. Celebrate full and more language.
4. Dump and try again.
items.teacherRole: Honor dump-and-fill play; narrate quantity without drilling.
items.teacherLanguage: How many dots? Can we put one apple for each?
items.observationOpportunities:
One-to-one vs handful dump
Notices fuller basket
Seeks help with dots
items.extensions: Deliver three apples to the dramatic-play market.
items.adaptations: Limit to baskets 1 and 2 only.
items.safetyNotes: Oversized counters only. Sweep floor apples to prevent slips.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher places first apple; child continues.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a 3-dot basket when ready.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers match numeral cards after dots.
items.cleanupTip: Count aloud while returning apples to the bin.

items.title: Pick the Apples
items.objective: Reach for apple props at two heights and carry them to a basket.
items.description: Movement orchard: tape or hang apple shapes low and high; gentle picking.
items.materials:
Paper or fabric apples
Baskets
Tape or low hooks
Optional music
items.setup: Place apples at floor and child-chest height. Clear pathways.
items.steps:
1. Model gentle pick and carry.
2. Children gather apples into baskets.
3. Pause for rest between rounds.
4. Sort into the big orchard tub.
items.teacherRole: Cue gentle hands; stop racing; spot near furniture.
items.teacherLanguage: Reach high. Soft pick. Two hands on the basket.
items.observationOpportunities:
Prefers low or high apples
Carry style
Stops when music pauses
items.extensions: Sort picked apples by color at the finish.
items.adaptations: Seated pick from a low crate for less locomotion.
items.safetyNotes: No climbing furniture. Keep pathways clear.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand a low apple directly; celebrate the carry.
items.additionalChallenge: Carry two apples without dropping.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers hang a few apples for friends.
items.cleanupTip: Two orchard helpers gather leftovers.

monday.teacherPreparation: Allergy list posted for Thursday. Adult-cut stamp apples before arrival. Stage investigation table fully.
monday.circleTime: Sing Crunch Goes the Apple once. Pass one whole apple for look-only. Preview stamp and pick games.
monday.activityFlow: Investigation → Stamp Painting → Count the Apples → Pick the Apples (short outdoor/indoor reach).
monday.questions: What do you notice on the apple? Is the skin cool or warm?
monday.observationFocus: Sensory approach or avoidance; gentle hands; dump-vs-place counting.
monday.familyConnection: Ask families to notice one grocery apple color or stem at home and share a word.
monday.outdoorPlay: Hang fabric apples on a low fence for gentle picking; shade for sticky stamp cleanup.
monday.observations: Notes who needs dry alternatives; who uses stem/skin words.
monday.adaptations: Sealed-bag apple for touch-averse children; seated pick option.
monday.safetyNotes: No tasting Monday. Adult prepares stamp cuts.

tuesday.theme: Colors We Can Sort, Tear, and Dance
tuesday.objectives:
Sort red/green/yellow props.
Tear paper for a process collage.
Freeze on color cues.
tuesday.materials:
Color baskets
Paper circles or props
Tear paper
Glue sticks
Scarves
tuesday.vocabulary:
Red
Green
Yellow
Apple
Color
Sort

items.title: Apple Color Sort
items.objective: Sort red, green, and yellow apple props into matching baskets.
items.description: Sample apple in each basket anchors the first sort.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow apple props or paper circles
Three baskets with color swatches
items.setup: Place one sample apple in each basket before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Name the sample colors.
2. Children sort remaining apples.
3. Narrate mismatches kindly.
4. Mix and sort again.
items.teacherRole: Accept size sorts first, then invite a color pass.
items.teacherLanguage: Does it match the sample? Red with red.
items.observationOpportunities:
Checks sample before placing
Strategy when one color runs out
items.extensions: Sort with eyes closed using textured paper apples.
items.adaptations: Begin with two colors only.
items.safetyNotes: No tiny sorting chips. Real apples are look-only during sort.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand the child only red apples first.
items.additionalChallenge: Add yellow on round two.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers label baskets with words.
items.cleanupTip: Sing a short apples-home chant into the storage tub.

items.title: Apple Peel Tear Collage
items.objective: Tear paper and stick pieces to build a process apple collage.
items.description: Children tear red, green, and yellow paper and glue pieces onto a soft circle guide—or ignore the guide.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow paper
Glue sticks
Trays
Optional light pencil circle
items.setup: Start one teacher tear on each tray. Glue sticks only.
items.steps:
1. Model a slow tear.
2. Children tear and stick freely.
3. Optional: add a brown paper stem.
4. Display process work—no matching model.
items.teacherRole: Protect tearing as the skill; refuse pre-cut squares as the main task.
items.teacherLanguage: Tear, tear—stick. Your apple can be messy!
items.observationOpportunities:
Tear style
Clusters vs covers
Asks for more paper
items.extensions: Dictate a one-word title for the collage.
items.adaptations: Pre-snipped starter tears; child continues tearing.
items.safetyNotes: No glitter. Watch paper near mouths.
items.supportAdaptations: Hold the paper while the child pulls.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a leaf torn from green paper.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers tear magazine color patches.
items.cleanupTip: Keep a scrap bowl for tomorrow’s collage.

items.title: Apple Color Dance
items.objective: Move or freeze when a color scarf cue is shown.
items.description: Short color-cue freezes with scarves—20–30 second rounds.
items.materials:
Red, green, yellow scarves or bandanas
Clear floor space
items.setup: Give each child one scarf color. Tape a dance circle if needed.
items.steps:
1. Hold up a color cue.
2. Matching scarves move; others freeze.
3. Switch cues quickly.
4. End with all colors dancing.
items.teacherRole: Keep rounds short; model exaggerated freeze.
items.teacherLanguage: Red moves! Green freezes. Listen with your eyes.
items.observationOpportunities:
Watches cue before moving
Freeze quality
Frustration with waiting
items.extensions: Add a drum tap for each color change.
items.adaptations: Partner a hesitant child with a teacher model.
items.safetyNotes: Scarves off necks. Clear furniture edges.
items.supportAdaptations: Only two colors in the first round.
items.additionalChallenge: Children take turns being the color caller.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers all move together without freeze.
items.cleanupTip: Toss scarves into a laundry basket like apple collecting.

tuesday.teacherPreparation: Print/cut color cards from the picture pack. Pre-tear one sample strip per tray.
tuesday.circleTime: Hold up three color cards. Children point to matching clothes or scarves.
tuesday.activityFlow: Color Sort → Apple Peel Tear Collage → Apple Color Dance.
tuesday.questions: Which basket matches this apple? What color did you tear first?
tuesday.observationFocus: Color matching strategy; tear strength; freeze control.
tuesday.familyConnection: Send a photo of the collage process (faces optional).
tuesday.outdoorPlay: Sidewalk chalk color circles as sort targets.
tuesday.observations: Who sorts by size first; who needs two-color start.
tuesday.adaptations: Two colors only for first sort; starter tears for collage.
tuesday.safetyNotes: Glue sticks only; scarves off necks.

wednesday.objectives:
Compare apple sizes.
Measure with yarn/cubes.
Roll bodies safely on mats.
wednesday.materials:
Sized apple props
Yarn
Cubes
Mats or blankets
wednesday.vocabulary:
Big
Small
Large
Little
Round
Compare

items.title: Big or Small?
items.objective: Compare clearly different apple sizes and sort into big/small.
items.description: Side-by-side size compare with obvious contrast before close calls.
items.materials:
Large and small apple props
Two baskets labeled with big/little circles
items.setup: Start with extreme size pairs only.
items.steps:
1. Hold two apples side by side.
2. Children choose big or small basket.
3. Invite disagreement and re-check.
4. Line biggest to smallest.
items.teacherRole: Welcome debate; avoid saying a child is wrong about close sizes.
items.teacherLanguage: Which feels bigger in your hands? Show me.
items.observationOpportunities:
Sight vs hand-weigh strategy
Invented size words
items.extensions: Build a bridge from biggest to smallest.
items.adaptations: Offer only two objects at a time.
items.safetyNotes: No hard throwing of real apples.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher holds both; child points.
items.additionalChallenge: Find a medium apple for a third basket.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers measure with yarn length.
items.cleanupTip: Store big and small in separate bins.

items.title: Apple Measuring Station
items.objective: Measure around or beside apples using yarn and cubes.
items.description: Non-standard measurement: wrap yarn or line cubes beside an apple.
items.materials:
Apples or props
Short yarn lengths
Linking cubes or Duplo
Trays
items.setup: Demonstrate wrapping yarn once, then hand yarn to the child.
items.steps:
1. Wrap or line up units.
2. Count cubes with pointing.
3. Compare which apple needs longer yarn.
4. Reset trays.
items.teacherRole: Hold apple steady when needed; keep yarn short.
items.teacherLanguage: Around the apple—how many cubes tall beside it?
items.observationOpportunities:
Yarn taut vs loose
One-to-one pointing on cubes
items.extensions: Graph longer/shorter with cube towers.
items.adaptations: Teacher wraps; child chooses which apple is longer.
items.safetyNotes: Yarn under 12 inches. Adult supervision.
items.supportAdaptations: Clip yarn to tray edge.
items.additionalChallenge: Measure a toy pumpkin vs apple.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers record tally marks.
items.cleanupTip: Wind yarn onto cardboard notches.

items.title: Roll Like an Apple
items.objective: Practice log rolls and curled rolls on mats.
items.description: Gross-motor apple play: log roll first, then curled apple roll.
items.materials:
Gym mats or folded blankets
Optional bean bags
Clear roll path
items.setup: Clear the path. Offer log rolls before curled rolls.
items.steps:
1. Model log roll.
2. Children roll across the mat.
3. Optional bean bag on belly.
4. Rest and try curled rolls.
items.teacherRole: Spot near walls; no head-first dives.
items.teacherLanguage: Curl small like an apple. Roll, roll—stop!
items.observationOpportunities:
Initiates vs waits
Head protection
Enjoys vs avoids floor
items.extensions: Roll to a basket and drop in one apple prop.
items.adaptations: Seated spin for children avoiding floor rolls.
items.safetyNotes: Clear path. Spot near walls. No diving.
items.supportAdaptations: Hand cue on shoulder to start roll.
items.additionalChallenge: Roll carrying a soft apple to the basket.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers rock side to side only.
items.cleanupTip: Two children stack mats from opposite ends.

wednesday.teacherPreparation: Cut yarn under 12 inches. Clear roll path. Set measuring trays.
wednesday.circleTime: Read or revisit Ten Apples Up On Top! with finger counting.
wednesday.activityFlow: Big or Small? → Apple Measuring Station → Roll Like an Apple.
wednesday.questions: Which apple needs the longer yarn? How do we keep heads safe when we roll?
wednesday.observationFocus: Size language; measuring attempts; roll initiation.
wednesday.familyConnection: Invite families to compare two fruits by size at home.
wednesday.outdoorPlay: Compare pinecones as big/small orchard props on dry grass.
wednesday.observations: Who debates size; who avoids floor rolls.
wednesday.safetyNotes: Short yarn; spot rolls near walls.

thursday.theme: Taste, Vote, and Open the Market
thursday.objectives:
Taste safely or help as non-taster.
Vote on a favorite graph.
Play apple market roles.
thursday.materials:
Allergy list
Tiny apple bits
Napkins
Graph paper
Market props
thursday.vocabulary:
Taste
Sweet
Crunchy
Juicy
Favorite
Healthy

items.title: Apple Taste Test
items.objective: Taste tiny apple pieces safely—or take a non-tasting helper role.
items.description: Allergy-aware tasting with equal status for non-tasters.
items.materials:
Adult-cut pea-sized apple bits
Color-coded napkins
Allergy list
Graph stickers
items.setup: Review allergy notes. Plate tiny bits. Offer smell plate for non-tasters.
items.steps:
1. Wash hands.
2. Smell, then optional taste.
3. Non-tasters serve napkins or place stickers.
4. Name sweet/tart favorites.
items.teacherRole: Guard allergy protocol; never pressure tasting.
items.teacherLanguage: Smell first. One tiny bite if you want. Helpers are important too.
items.observationOpportunities:
Spit/swallow/hold
Chooses helper role
Points to favorite napkin
items.extensions: Place sticker on class favorite chart.
items.adaptations: Lick a clean spoon that touched apple for texture-sensitive children.
items.safetyNotes: Allergy protocol first. Adult prepares cuts. Watch each bite. No sharing bites.
items.supportAdaptations: Smell-only plate with equal celebration.
items.additionalChallenge: Describe tart vs sweet to a friend.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help pass napkins.
items.cleanupTip: Compost scraps; sanitize table twice.

items.title: Favorite Apple Graph
items.objective: Place a sticker on a favorite apple-color column—including non-tasters.
items.description: Picture-card headers; every child votes, including look-only choosers.
items.materials:
Butcher paper columns
Apple color picture cards
Stickers
items.setup: Post three columns with picture-card headers—not children’s faces.
items.steps:
1. Review colors.
2. Each child places one sticker.
3. Count the tallest column together.
4. Photograph for families.
items.teacherRole: Include non-tasters in ‘looks yummy’ columns; avoid pressure.
items.teacherLanguage: Which column is yours today? Let’s clap for the tallest.
items.observationOpportunities:
Counts spontaneously
Changes mind after peers
Includes non-taster role
items.extensions: Clap once per sticker in the tallest column.
items.adaptations: Offer hand-over-hand sticker placement when fine motor is emerging.
items.safetyNotes: Stickers off mouths. Avoid food-look stickers.
items.supportAdaptations: Offer only two columns.
items.additionalChallenge: Children dictate a caption for the graph photo.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers write tallies.
items.cleanupTip: Photograph, then roll the paper.

items.title: Apple Market
items.objective: Buy and sell apple props using simple polite phrases.
items.description: Small stocked stand so children practice restocking, not hoarding.
items.materials:
Toy or fabric apples
Baskets
Muffin-tin drawer
Paper coin circles
items.setup: Stock only a few apples. Model one phrase, then step out.
items.steps:
1. Open the market.
2. Take turns as seller/customer.
3. Restock from the orchard tub.
4. Close with a sold-out sign.
items.teacherRole: Model ‘How many apples today?’ once; coach turn-taking.
items.teacherLanguage: How many apples today? Please. Thank you.
items.observationOpportunities:
Role preference
Turn-taking at register
Uses please/thank you
items.extensions: Deliver a basket to block-area neighbors.
items.adaptations: Picture menu for pointing orders.
items.safetyNotes: Coins larger than choke tubes. No real coins.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher plays customer first.
items.additionalChallenge: Price apples as 1 or 2 coins.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers write open/closed signs.
items.cleanupTip: Sort props by type under the sold-out sign.

thursday.teacherPreparation: Confirm allergies. Cut pea-sized bits. Post graph with picture-card headers.
thursday.activityFlow: Taste Test → Favorite Apple Graph → Apple Market.
thursday.questions: Sweet or tart? Which column gets your sticker today?
thursday.observationFocus: Tasting comfort; equal helper status; market turn-taking.
thursday.familyConnection: Share graph photo and one tasting word (or helper pride note).
thursday.outdoorPlay: Blanket market under a tree with wagon deliveries.
thursday.observations: Who chooses helper role; polite phrases at market.
thursday.adaptations: Smell-only plate; picture menu for orders.
thursday.safetyNotes: Allergy protocol; no sharing bites; oversized coins.

friday.objectives:
Order growth cards.
Look at seeds safely.
Make process trees.
Celebrate with a short parade.
friday.materials:
Growth cards
Apple half for looking
Seed jar
Tree art supplies
Scarves
friday.vocabulary:
Tree
Orchard
Branch
Leaf
Blossom
Seed
Grow
Harvest

items.title: Apple Life Cycle
items.objective: Put apple growth cards in order from seed to ripe apple.
items.description: Left-to-right story with picture-card pack growth sequence.
items.materials:
Amazing Apples growth cards
Tray
Optional painter’s tape arrow
items.setup: Show order once, mix cards, invite repair of the story.
items.steps:
1. Say the story together.
2. Mix cards.
3. Children reorder.
4. Act out seed-to-tree with bodies.
items.teacherRole: Keep language story-like; avoid quiz pressure.
items.teacherLanguage: What comes after the seed? Then the little tree…
items.observationOpportunities:
Places seed before tree
Story language while ordering
items.extensions: Match cards to a real potted seedling if available.
items.adaptations: Offer first/last cards only; adult fills middle with child approval.
items.safetyNotes: Laminate cards. No loose seeds as manipulatives.
items.supportAdaptations: Two-card choice only.
items.additionalChallenge: Child teaches the order to a friend.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers add blossom card.
items.cleanupTip: Rubber-band each set in order.

items.title: Apple Seed Discovery
items.objective: Look at seeds inside an adult-cut apple half.
items.description: Supervised looking: adult cuts and holds; seeds go into a sealed jar after.
items.materials:
Adult-cut apple half
Observation tray
Sealed clear jar
Optional view-finder
items.setup: Cut away from children. Display half on tray; jar ready for seeds.
items.steps:
1. Look and point.
2. Count seeds together if calm.
3. Seal seeds in the jar.
4. Compost the fruit scrap.
items.teacherRole: Keep tools away from children; narrate inside/outside.
items.teacherLanguage: The seeds were inside. We look—we don’t eat the seeds.
items.observationOpportunities:
Points without grabbing
Compares to other seeds known
items.extensions: Plant one seed in a cup for a week-long watch.
items.adaptations: Dry picture card for children who dislike wet fruit.
items.safetyNotes: Adult prepares the cut away from children. Seeds are not snacks.
items.supportAdaptations: Watch from a second chair with the picture card.
items.additionalChallenge: Draw the seed jar in a science journal.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help wipe the tray.
items.cleanupTip: Seal seeds; sanitize tools away from children.

items.title: My Apple Tree
items.objective: Build a process apple tree with trunk and fingerprint or pom-pom apples.
items.description: Child-taped trunk strip plus messy apples—no identical sticker rows.
items.materials:
Brown paper trunk strips
Green paper or paint
Red fingerprint paint or large pom-poms
Glue
items.setup: Offer trunks children tape themselves. Put out fingerprint pads or pom-poms.
items.steps:
1. Tape trunk.
2. Add leaves.
3. Add apples freely.
4. Dictate a one-line story.
items.teacherRole: Refuse adult-perfect trees; celebrate all-over apples.
items.teacherLanguage: Where will your apples grow? Top, bottom, everywhere?
items.observationOpportunities:
Apples only at top vs all over
Narrates pickers
items.extensions: Family caption from dictated story.
items.adaptations: Larger pom-poms for grasp.
items.safetyNotes: Washable non-toxic paint. Pom-poms larger than choke tubes.
items.supportAdaptations: Pre-taped trunk; child adds apples only.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a sun or basket under the tree.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers tear leaves themselves.
items.cleanupTip: Close paint pads; pom-poms in mesh wash bag.

items.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
items.objective: Share one apple word and parade once around the rug.
items.description: Closing circle: vocabulary share, short parade, scarf or streamer wave.
items.materials:
Scarves or streamers
Optional music or LLH chant
Graph photo
items.setup: Keep parade path to one rug loop.
items.steps:
1. Each child shares one apple word (opt-in).
2. Chant together.
3. One loop parade.
4. Wave to the graph photo.
items.teacherRole: Keep energy walking-feet; honor silent waves.
items.teacherLanguage: What apple word will you share? Harvest parade—walking feet.
items.observationOpportunities:
Which words return
Who wants to lead
Regulation in parade
items.extensions: Thank kitchen staff who washed apples.
items.adaptations: Flag wave from a chair instead of marching.
items.safetyNotes: No running parade. Streamers away from faces.
items.supportAdaptations: Whisper share to teacher only.
items.additionalChallenge: Child leads one verse of the chant.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce with scarves in arms.
items.cleanupTip: End with graph/art photo for families.

friday.teacherPreparation: Rubber-band card sets. Cut apple away from children. Stage art.
friday.circleTime: Retell seed-to-apple with cards. Practice harvest chant.
friday.activityFlow: Life Cycle → Seed Discovery → My Apple Tree → Harvest Celebration.
friday.questions: What comes after the seed? What apple word will you share?
friday.observationFocus: Sequencing language; look-only seed safety; parade regulation.
friday.familyConnection: Send tree art photo and favorite vocabulary from the week.
friday.outdoorPlay: Parade to the garden fence and back; match cards to a seedling if present.
friday.observations: Who retells growth order; who leads parade calmly.
friday.adaptations: First/last cards only; chair flag wave.
friday.safetyNotes: Adult cut only; seeds sealed; walking feet in parade.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:wednesday:.imageRequirementReason: Two baskets with size labels are ordinary classroom sorting.

paper signs with a big circle and a little circle instead of words

week.weeklyOverview: Toddlers explore real apples through looking, sorting, moving, tasting (with allergy care), and process art. Each day adds one new way to know an apple—never the same stamp-and-sort loop twice.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Whole apples (red, green, yellow)
Apple halves for stamping (adult-cut)
Washable paint
Chunky plastic or fabric apples
Baskets and shoebox bins
Dot number cards
Yarn and linking cubes
Scarves
Butcher paper
Glue sticks
Picture card pack (draft PDF)
Napkins and sanitizer
Magnifying tools or view-finders
Gym mats or blankets
week.teacherPreparation: Confirm allergy notes before Thursday tasting. Adult-cut stamp apples Monday morning. Print and cut the Amazing Apples Picture Card Pack. Stage one center fully before children arrive; keep backup props in a closed tub.
week.familyConnection: Ask families to notice an apple at home or store—color, stem, or crunch—and send one word or photo of a grocery apple (no child faces required).
milestones: Language: Uses sensory and color words about apples
SEL: Accepts non-tasting roles during the taste test
Cognition: Sorts by color or size with purpose
Motor: Presses stamps, tears paper, carries baskets
Creativity: Makes process art without a matching model

songs.title: Crunch Goes the Apple (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original Little Learner Hub chant written for this lesson; not derived from a commercial recording.
songs.lyrics:
Crunch goes the apple, crunch crunch crunch.
I hold it careful—munch munch munch.
Red or green or yellow bright,
I taste my apple—just one bite!
songs.motions: Tap fists together for crunch; mime holding; point to colors; pretend one careful bite.
songs.teacherDirections: Chant slowly before tasting. Offer a silent mouth movement for non-tasters.
songs.whenToUse: Thursday before the taste test and Friday celebration.

songs.title: Apple Seeds Wiggle (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH fingerplay written for Amazing Apples toddler week to replace uncertain traditional fingerplays. Not adapted from a copyrighted recording.
songs.lyrics:
Tiny apple seeds inside,
Wiggle, wiggle—then we hide.
Stretch up tall like apple trees,
Shake one branch—soft as you please.
songs.motions: Curl small; wiggle fingers; cover eyes briefly; stretch tall; gentle arm shake.
songs.teacherDirections: Use before life-cycle or seed looking. Keep shakes soft.
songs.whenToUse: Friday before Apple Life Cycle / Seed Discovery.

songs.title: Basket Fill (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH transition chant created for toddler apple sorting and cleanup.
songs.lyrics:
Fill, fill, fill the basket—
Red one, green one, in they go.
Pat the basket, nice and steady,
Apples ready—here we go!
songs.motions: Pretend place apples; pat basket; march two steps.
songs.teacherDirections: Use during cleanup of Count the Apples and Color Sort.

books.title: Ten Apples Up On Top!
books.author: Theo LeSieg (Dr. Seuss)
books.verificationSource: Penguin Random House / Beginner Books listing for ISBN 9780394800196 credits Theo. LeSieg (Dr. Seuss pseudonym), illustrated by Roy McKie: https://www.penguinrandomhouseretail.com/book/?isbn=9780394800196 — ages commonly early reader / adult-paced for toddlers.
books.ageSuitability: Toddler–early preschool (short rhythmic text; adult paces pages)
books.whyThisBook: Playful counting with apples supports Count the Apples without requiring worksheets.
beforeReadingQuestions: What do you think will happen if more apples go on top?
duringReadingPrompts: Can you show me three with your fingers?
afterReadingQuestions: Should we stack pretend apples on our heads or only on the floor today?
books.substituteTitle: No book: count plastic apples onto a plate while chanting numbers.
